resources.string: PVB speaker correction (runs after JamesDSP effects when on)

When the correction is off, plays the original sound matched to the recent playback loudness. It starts from an estimate and updates with a 10 s average. While virtual bass is in use, the same delay is kept for fair comparison. JamesDSP effects still apply before it. If this is off as well, JamesDSP processing is used alone.
Bypassed automatically on earphones and Bluetooth
Output level (raise the volume by the same amount)
The lower the volume, the more the low-mids are boosted. Off by default until the volume table is measured
Extra boost per dB of volume reduction
Raises the low-mids slightly only in quiet passages where the phone limiter has headroom. Moves slowly over 0.5 to 1 s
Maximum extra boost in quiet passages
Level where the extra boost starts (higher = more often)
Adds fullness and weight to the bass: pick a mode or set the model and strength yourself. All models add about 0.15 s of delay

This feature is still being compared by ear.

• The bass effect and any harshness depend on the song.
• If you hear buzzing or a mechanical sound, lower the virtual bass strength or try the "More fullness" mode. The "Deep bass" mode can buzz on songs with dense bass.
• All models add about 0.15 s of delay.

When comparing models, listen at the same strength.
When you change the virtual bass strength (including mode and model) while a song plays, it is remembered for that song and applied again next time. Reading the song needs notification access.

Tap to open the settings and allow notification access for this app. Without it the song is unknown and the default strength is always used.
Can be turned on in the virtual bass card. While off, nothing is remembered or applied. Remembered songs are kept.

Changing the strength while a song plays remembers it for that song and applies it when the song plays again. Songs without a memory, and no song playing, use the default strength (%1$s). Up to 500 songs are remembered; beyond that the song not heard for the longest time is removed first.
Delete the memory of \"%1$s\"? If it is playing now, the default strength is used again.
Delete all %1$d remembered songs? This cannot be undone.

Lowers the virtual bass strength automatically as the volume goes up. At high volume the bass protection limiter of the phone acts first, so more strength does not make the bass louder but squeezes the mids and muddies the sound. The slider value above stays as it is; it is only reduced during playback.
Volume %1$s%% → %2$s (applied strength %3$s)\nFrom %4$s%%, reduces by %5$s dB per 1%%, at most %6$s dB.
Volume %1$s%% → no reduction (applied strength %2$s)\nFrom %3$s%%, reduces by %4$s dB per 1%%, at most %5$s dB.
Higher starts reducing at a louder volume, so the virtual bass is reduced less at the same volume.

Higher allows more reduction of the virtual bass at very high volume.

Off by default. In the developer\'s listening the difference was small or none, but they may sound different to other people and on other phones, so they are here to try. They only work while virtual bass is on, and all four only reduce the virtual bass, never raise it, so the bass may sound a little smaller with them on.
Pushes down short swells of the virtual bass to reduce a “hoong-hoong” wobble. Right after a new note starts it is briefly quieter.
Lets the virtual bass come in over about 0.15 s on kicks and new notes instead of jumping up at once.

Only with the “More fullness” mode. Joins each harmonic\'s level changes into one envelope so harmonics drop out and back in less, and lowers the virtual bass by 2 dB to make up for it getting larger. Sound pauses briefly when switched.
Lowers the virtual bass by up to 6 dB while the mids and highs (500–4000 Hz) are busier than usual for the song.
Tell us whether you hear a difference or not. The song, the volume and which options were on help.\ngithub.com/ksysh3-dot/rootnote/issues
